papers.title: Frictional behavior between bone and additively manufactured Ti6Al4V implants is affected by bone density and surface texture under varying loads
papers.abstract: Friction at the bone-implant interface is a key factor in the initial stability of cementless orthopedic implants, largely affecting their long-term osseointegration behavior. Yet, there is limited data available for coefficients of friction (COFs) of different combinations of bone qualities and implant surface morphologies, particularly those produced by additive manufacturing techniques. This study measured the interfacial COFs of combinations of three levels of human cancellous bone qualities, characterized based on the BMD, and four Ti6Al4V micro and macro surface textures, produced using selective laser melting (SLM), under three levels of normal stress (0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 MPa), using a reciprocal friction test apparatus. Results indicated a wide range for the COF (0.37-0.95), significantly influenced by the individual effect of each of the metal surface roughness (strong positive: P-value < 0.05 and F-value = 19.12), bone density (moderate negative: P-value < 0.05 and F-value = 7.22) and normal stress (strong negative: P-value < 0.05 and F-value = 40.63), but not the interaction effects. A more variable frictional behavior was observed for both a lower density bone and a sharper-edged metallic texture, presumably due to the higher ploughing inconsistencies involved. The findings highlight the capability of SLM for developing COF-tailored patient-specific implants, based on personalized bone properties and biomechanical considerations.

summary_en.motivation: Limited data exists on coefficients of friction for combinations of bone quality and additively manufactured implant surface textures, which are critical for initial stability.
summary_en.method: Reciprocal friction tests were conducted with human cancellous bone of three bone mineral density levels and four SLM-produced Ti6Al4V surface textures under three normal stresses.
summary_en.result: Coefficients of friction ranged from 0.37 to 0.95, significantly influenced by surface roughness (positive), bone density (negative), and normal stress (negative), with no significant interaction effects.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through experimental friction measurements using actual human bone specimens and additively manufactured Ti6Al4V samples.

papers.title: An Analytical Framework for Correlation Between Laser Powder Bed Fusion Factors and Porosity-Induced Fracture Strength and Plasticity
papers.abstract: Strain-stress properties of additively manufactured materials by laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) are substantially determined by the porosity level that is generated during the additive manufacturing. Accordingly, to optimally design of the LPBFed sample addressing the best stress-strain behavior, the porosity levels should be optimized through adjustment of process factors. In order to do so, in the present work, an integrated multi-physics-based analytical model has been developed to firstly correlate the LPBF process factors to porosity level using the mechanism of melt pool formation, vapor depression and identifying the lack-of-fusion. Then, the calculated porosity is used as an input of continuum damage mechanics model namely Gurson–Tvergaard–Needleman (GTN) to predict the stress-strain behavior. Through this hybrid approach, stress-strain curves together with ultimate tensile stress, elongation at peak and elongation at break have been successfully calculated and correlated to LPBF process factors. To verify the results, the LPBF samples made of stainless steel 316 L were subjected to micro-CT analysis and tensile testing and the measured values of porosity and stress-strain curves compared to the modded values. Also, comparisons were made on experimental values of porosity, UTS and elongation of other 3D printed materials i.e. Ti6Al4V, Inconel 718 and AlSi10Mg which reported in the literature with the values obtained from integrated framework in this research. The results based on relative root mean square error (RRMSE) showed that the developed model has excellent to good prediction accuracy with RRMSE values varies between the 3% to 20% accuracy in prediction of porosity, UTS and elongation of stainless steel 316 L, Ti6Al4V and Inconel 718. Also, for the aluminum alloy the RRMSE varies between 20% and 30% that shows the prediction accuracy is fair.

papers.title: Effect of Copper Addition to Titanium Alloy Prepared By Additive Manufacturing for Biomedical Applications
papers.abstract: Infection remains one of the most serious complications in orthopedic and dental implants, and the ongoing search for effective solutions to reduce infection rates has been a focal point of research for decades. The challenge is to create a material with inherent antibacterial properties that do not compromise other essential biomaterial qualities. This study aimed to develop and characterize a novel material based on the widely used Ti-6Al-4V alloy commonly employed in orthopedic and dental medicine. Copper was added as an antimicrobial agent and an essential element in the human body, aiming to promote an intrinsic antibacterial ability of the material. The Ti-6Al-4V alloy was produced using additive manufacturing via laser-based direct energy deposition (DED-LB). A laser is applied to melt the locally fed Ti-6Al-4V metal powder and fuse it with the previously deposited layer. The Ti-6Al-4V- x Cu alloy was also produced using DED-LB, but copper powder was added to the Ti-6Al-4V powder. Materials characterization was performed using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), X-ray diffraction (XRD) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). Electrochemical tests were conducted in simulated physiological solutions (Hanks balanced salt solution, 0.9 wt.% sodium chloride and artificial saliva). Commercially available wrought Ti-6Al-4V alloy, produced by conventional metallurgical methods, was used as a reference (1). The microstructure and corrosion resistance of alloys manufactured by DED-LB have been addressed less extensively than those produced by power bed fusion processes. The composition, structure and electrochemical behaviour of Ti-6Al-4V alloy produced by two different methods: (i) wrought alloy produced by conventional metallurgy and (ii) additively manufactured (AM) alloy produced by DED-LB from Ti-6Al-4V without and with Cu powders were studied. Although the wrought and AM Ti-6Al-4V alloys shared identical chemical compositions, they exhibited distinct microstructures. The wrought alloy featured an α-phase matrix with intergranular β-phase, whereas the AM-produced alloys presented a lamellar Widmanstätten structure. Adding copper to the Ti-6Al-4V alloy reflected changes in the alloy’s microstructure and chemical composition. Both wrought, and DED-LB Ti-6Al-4V alloys exhibited passivation in the simulated physiological solution and showed no signs of localized corrosion. Moreover, the addition of copper did not compromise the alloy’s protective behavior in the simulated solutions, as confirmed by the long-term immersion and osseointegration tests. These results demonstrate that the properties of both DED-LB-produced Ti-6Al-4V and Ti-6Al-4V-Cu alloys are comparable to the commercial wrought alloy, highlighting their potential for further investigation regarding corrosion resistance and biological performance. papers.title: Effect of Cryo-Rolling on the Microstructural Evolution and Mechanical Properties of Ti-6Al-4V Alloy
papers.abstract: Ti-6Al-4V is valued for its strength-to-weight ratio in engineering applications. Cryo-rolling at sub-zero temperatures enhances strength and hardness through grain refinement and dislocation build-up. The present study investigates the role of cryo-rolling on the microstructural characteristics and mechanical properties of the alloy, which undergoes various degrees of deformation followed by heating at 900 °C for selected samples. Microstructural analysis reveals grain elongation, sub-grain formation, deformation bands, and dislocation densification with increasing thickness reduction. Twinning dominates deformation at low strain, while dislocation slips take over at high strain because of the decrease in grain size, which makes the formation of new twins progressively more challenging. No metastable phase appears during cryo-rolling or heat treatment, as confirmed by X-ray diffraction. Cryo-rolled samples exhibit about 45% and 29% reduction in grain size and crystallite size, and 160% intensification in dislocation density. This leads to rises of 19%, 23%, and 10% in yield strength, tensile strength, and hardness, respectively, while ductility remains nearly constant across all cryo-rolled conditions. Cryo-rolling inhibits dynamic recovery and recrystallisation, so strengthening mainly results from grain refinement and dislocation accumulation. These findings suggest that cryo-rolling can improve the strength and hardness of Ti-6Al-4V, while maintaining ductility and providing new processing insights.
